01 — I16, the journal since a date Audit-Journal · 390 px

I16, a time filter on the audit journal. GET /api/v1/journal gains since= the way the delta reads take it (SinceParam's parse_page/1: a date, an instant or the cursor a full page answered as as_of). The page takes the same parameter in its URL, so a link the agent hands over (/journal?since=2026-10-28) opens the slice it read.

Q1 — the control: A, one date field „Seit“ in the filter form beside the kind. B (a chip family „Zeitraum“: Alle · Heute · 7 Tage · 30 Tage) is drawn for contrast. A comment „Q1 B“ flips it.

dashed = new or changed · amber edge = an invented figure (the seed's window has no such booking total worked out) · 1 ties a change to its section's text. Synthetic data only.

The journal's time filter

1The field is a native date input (a tap and a pick on a phone), named since in the form the page already sends on every change; empty means no cut. 2The basis line names the cut in its existing clause order, after „Neueste zuerst“.

Q1, recommended A. (1) Any cut the agent hands over shows as itself. A link with since=2026-10-28 has no chip in B; B would need a fifth, „custom“ state that shows a date anyway. (2) One parameter, one control: the API's since and the field are the same value, so the basis line and the agent's read state the same cut. (3) No second chip row on a phone, where the actor and operation families already wrap.

The page stays newest first within the cut; the API, given since, answers oldest first with a cursor, as every paged delta read does (K17). Same rows, a different order, deliberately: a screen answers „what changed this week“, a poller walks forward. Without since both stay as today. The seed's entries are all from the day it ran, so the cut drops none here.
